title: Replace Elements with Greatest Element on Right Side
spaceBreakdown:
- int maxSoFar: single variable → O(1)
- int cur: single variable → O(1)
- not counted: input vector (modified in place), returned vector (same object)
approach: Iterate from right to left, maintaining the maximum value seen so far (initialized to -1). At each index, save the current element, replace it with the running maximum, then update the running maximum with the saved element. This works because the greatest element to the right of index i is simply the maximum of arr[i+1] and the greatest element to the right of index i+1, so a single right-to-left pass suffices.
hints: If you know the greatest element to the right of index i+1, what is the only other value you need to determine the greatest element to the right of index i?
Use a single right-to-left pass keeping a running maximum. For arr = [17,18,5,4,6,1], start at index 5 with max = -1: place -1 at index 5, then update max to max(-1, 1) = 1 and move left.

```
max_so_far = -1
for i from last index down to 0:
    cur = arr[i]
    arr[i] = max_so_far
    max_so_far = max(max_so_far, cur)
return arr
```

**Single element** - only one element, so there is nothing to its right.
`Input: arr = [400]` → `Expected: [-1]`
⚠️ Bug: initialising maxSoFar to 0 instead of -1 → returns `[0]`

**All equal values** - every element is the same, so each replacement is that same value except the last.
`Input: arr = [5,5,5]` → `Expected: [5,5,-1]`
⚠️ Bug: updating maxSoFar before assigning it to arr[i] (swapping the two inner lines) → returns `[5,5,5]`

**Reverse sorted** - each element is already the maximum of everything to its right.
`Input: arr = [5,4,3,2,1]` → `Expected: [5,4,3,2,-1]`
⚠️ Bug: iterating left-to-right instead of right-to-left → returns `[4,3,2,1,-1]` (uses left-neighbour instead of right-maximum)

**Boundary last element** - the last index must always become -1 regardless of its value.
`Input: arr = [1]` → `Expected: [-1]`
⚠️ Bug: loop starting at i = n-2 (skipping the last element) → returns `[1]`

followUps.q: Replace every element with the k-th greatest element to its right (or -1 if fewer than k elements remain). How does the approach change?
followUps.a: A running maximum alone is insufficient; you need to track the top-k elements seen so far. Maintain a sorted structure (e.g. a multiset or a min-heap of size k) of all elements to the right. At each index, the answer is the smallest element in that structure (the k-th largest), then insert the current element. TC becomes O(n log k), SC O(k).

followUps.q: Replace every element with the greatest element within the next k positions to its right (not all the way to the end). How does this change the solution?
followUps.a: This becomes a sliding-window maximum problem. Use a monotonic deque that stores indices in decreasing value order, evicting indices that fall outside the window [i+1, i+k]. TC O(n), SC O(k).

followUps.q: The array arrives as a stream from left to right and you must output each replacement immediately. Is this possible?
followUps.a: No - the replacement for index i depends on elements at indices i+1 through n-1, which have not arrived yet. You would need to buffer the entire stream first (O(n) memory) or receive the stream from right to left, in which case the original O(1)-space approach works unchanged.
